In [[geometry]], the '''icosahedral honeycomb''' is one of four compact, [[List of regular polytopes and compounds|regular]], [[Space-filling geometry|space-filling]] [[tessellation]]s (or [[honeycomb (geometry)|honeycombs]]) in [[Hyperbolic space|hyperbolic 3-space]]. With [[Schläfli symbol]] {{math|{3,5,3},}} there are three [[regular icosahedron|icosahedra]] around each [[Edge (geometry)|edge]], and 12 icosahedra around each [[Vertex (geometry)|vertex]], in a regular [[regular dodecahedron|dodecahedral]] [[vertex figure]]. It is analogous to the [[24-cell]] and the [[5-cell]].

{{Honeycomb}}

==Description==
The [[dihedral angle]] of a [[regular icosahedron]] is around 138.2°, so it is impossible to fit three icosahedra around an edge in Euclidean 3-space. However, in hyperbolic space, properly scaled icosahedra can have dihedral angles of exactly 120 degrees, so three of those can fit around an edge.

[[Image:Hyperb icosahedral hc.png|200px|thumb|Honeycomb seen in perspective outside Poincare's model disk]]

== Related regular honeycombs ==
There are four regular compact honeycombs in 3D hyperbolic space:
{{Regular compact H3 honeycombs}}

== Related regular polytopes and honeycombs ==
It is a member of a sequence of [[regular polychora]] and honeycombs {3,''p'',3} with [[deltahedron|deltrahedral]] cells:
{{Symmetric_tessellations}}

It is also a member of a sequence of [[regular polychora]] and honeycombs {''p'',5,''p''}, with [[vertex figure]]s composed of pentagons:
{{Symmetric4 tessellations}}

== Uniform honeycombs ==

There are [[Convex uniform honeycombs in hyperbolic space#.5B3.2C5.2C3.5D family|nine uniform honeycombs]] in the [3,5,3] [[Coxeter group]] family, including this regular form as well as the [[Bitruncation (geometry)|bitruncated]] form, t<sub>1,2</sub>{3,5,3}, {{CDD|node|3|node_1|5|node_1|3|node}}, also called ''truncated dodecahedral honeycomb'', each of whose cells are [[truncated dodecahedron|truncated dodecahedra]].
{{353 family}}

The '''partially diminished icosahedral honeycomb''' or '''[[parabidiminished icosahedron|parabidiminished icosahedral]] honeycomb''', pd{3,5,3}, is a non-Wythoffian uniform honeycomb with [[regular dodecahedron|dodecahedron]] and [[pentagonal antiprism]] cells, with a tetrahedrally diminished dodecahedron vertex figure. The icosahedral cells of the {3,5,3} are [[diminishment (geometry)|diminished]] at opposite vertices (parabidiminished), leaving a [[pentagonal antiprism]] ([[parabidiminished icosahedron]]) core, and creating new dodecahedron cells above and below.<ref>Wendy Y. Krieger, Walls and bridges: The view from six dimensions, ''Symmetry: Culture and Science'' Volume 16, Number 2, pages 171–192 (2005) [https://www.os2fan2.com/gloss/wb4.pdf pdf] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007060826/http://symmetry.hu/content/aus_journal_content_abs_2005_16_2.html|date=2013-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/pt353.htm|title = Pd{3,5,3}|author=Dr. Richard Klitzing|publisher=bendwavy.org}}</ref>
